blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 48 in June to 45 in October (−6.2%), and it took 5.4% of the city’s 294 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 42 in June to 34 in October (−19.0%), and it took 7.2% of the city’s 456 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out Morgan Creek for detached houses in June, July, October (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in July, September (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June (a buyers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: It links out to the separate Morgan Creek homes-for-sale page.

Identity call: Morgan Creek is the established South Surrey golf-course community of larger lots and custom-built homes around 32 Avenue / 160 Street, centred on the Morgan Creek Golf Course, near White Rock Beach, Highway 99 and the U.S.

Morgan Heights is also a separate place — south of 28 Avenue and west of 164 Street, a newer neighbourhood planned in 2005 in Grandview Heights — and is not part of the Morgan Creek golf-course community.
OCP — Surrey: Local plans for this area: Rosemary Heights Central NCP, Rosemary Heights West NCP and Rosemary Heights Business Park Plan.

ALR block: subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error, and no farm-class claim is asserted for this area.

South of 28 Avenue and west of 164 Street, planned in 2005 in Grandview Heights — neither Morgan Creek nor Morgan Crossing. Listings using a bare "Morgan" name need the sub-area checked before any comparison is drawn.

faq.a: No. Morgan Creek is the golf-course community around 32 Avenue / 160 Street with its own board row (Detached 45 / 5 / 11%; Condos & Townhomes 39 / 9 / 23% in September 2026); Morgan Crossing is the separate retail village at 24 Avenue / 160 Street in Grandview Heights, whose ground uses the Grandview board row.
faq.q: Is Morgan Creek the same as Morgan Crossing?

faq.a: On MLS®, yes — the Morgan Creek sub-area includes both the golf course neighbourhood and Rosemary Heights, while the City treats Rosemary Heights as its own planning area with Central and West neighbourhood concept plans.
faq.q: Is Rosemary Heights part of Morgan Creek?

faq.a: Up to 3 units on lots smaller than 280 m², 4 units on lots larger than 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop (Surrey changes adopted July 8, 2024).
faq.q: How many units can a Morgan Creek lot hold under SSMUH?

faq.a: Its habitable floor area may not exceed 40% of the principal dwelling unit's habitable floor area, one suite per dwelling unit, and it is not a separate strata lot.
